design_rationale:
WORKLOG — task 0 of membership_benefits_desk (Northbeam Circle membership benefits desk). Revision 2,
rewritten after the source-layer audit at
env/env_0005_consumer_electronics_retailer/audits/policy_task/membership_benefits_desk/ returned RED on all four
relationships. Every figure below is from the revision-2 harness run recorded under STEP 5.

STEP 0. DRAW AND ASSET LEDGER.
scripts/draw_counts.py env/env_0005_consumer_electronics_retailer/tasks/membership_benefits_desk --tasks 2 printed, for
task 0: {"task": 0, "prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [6, 5, 6]}; for task 1:
{"task": 1, "prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [5, 6, 4]}. Task 0 is a tree of two
prerequisite problems besides the root, and its three computations carry 5, 6 and 6 declared factors:
membership_ext_grace_dues_settlement 5, membership_ext_year_benefit_credit_grant 6,
membership_ext_benefit_credit_application 6. Task 0 claims the benefit-credit side of the desk: the member's own
settlement of the dues standing on the membership, the grant of the membership year's service credit, and the
application of that credit against one charge. Reserved untouched for task 1: the whole reward-points side.
Neither task reuses the other's event types: task 0 writes membership_dues_payment, membership_benefit_grant and
membership_benefit_redeem; task 1 writes membership_points_accrue, membership_points_expire and
membership_points_redeem.

DESIGN THESIS. Surface goal the customer volunteers: "I have a repair bill from your engineer and I was told my
Circle membership covers some of it — can you put it against this repair bill?" Scored core parameter: the
benefit credit set against that repair bill (75.15). Two problems stand between the goal and that figure, neither
mentioned by the customer. (1) The credit set against a charge is worked out only after the ledger carries, for
the membership year in which that charge falls, a grant of the very named benefit that charge's kind calls for —
the charge is repair labour, so the benefit its kind calls for is the service credit, and the year that began on
1 September 2026 carries grants under the install and delivery credits only. (2) The credit granted for a
membership year is worked out only after the dues charged for the billing period the membership is now in stand
met in full by the payments applied to that period — 179.99 was charged on 1 September and only 60.00 has been
applied, so the grant is 187.80 rather than 242.80 until the member settles. Depth: surface goal -> the credit
standing under the named benefit -> the year's grant -> how the year's dues stand -> the member's own
settlement. Breadth: the three computations read, in parallel, the membership dues ledger, the benefit grant and
redemption ledger, the points-accrual ledger, the ShieldCare plan with its premium and payout ledgers, the
TechWorks agreement with its labour, parts, trip and visit ledgers, the Northbeam credit account with its store
credit postings, and the return authorisation with the fee waived on it and the refund still standing to the member.

WHY THE CUSTOMER'S OWN WRITE IS THE SETTLEMENT. The charter divides the desk's actions between service actions
taken for a verified member and acts that dispose of the member's own position, which are handed over. Money
leaving the member's own card is the plainest case of the second kind: the desk can work out what is owed, read
it back and unlock the payment, but it cannot authorise a charge on the member's card for her — she does that
herself, and she does it on the call, which is why it is completable inside one frozen_time (the card is on
file, the receipt is immediate, and nothing clears afterwards for the write to depend on). What stays with the
agent is the retailer's own bookkeeping around it: granting credit and spending granted credit against a charge,
which are this task's other two writes.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD.
- membership_dues_billing governs the settlement's subject membership_dues_payment. Its one gate,
  billable_membership_state ("Dues are billed, and payments applied, only while the membership record stands in
  application_received, active or grace"), kind=state, correlation membership_holdings.membership_id -> the
  action's membership_id. At frozen_time the record stands in grace, so the gate holds. Its allocation clause —
  "A payment is applied to the oldest unpaid billing period first, and any remainder to the next" — is inherited
  in full and the extended rule repeats it verbatim; the world is laid out so that the oldest unpaid billing
  period IS the one beginning 2026-09-01 (the 2025 period was charged 179.99 plus a 9.00 late fee and paid
  179.99 plus 9.00; the proration period beginning 2026-05-15 was charged 32.50 plus a 9.00 late fee and paid 41.50), so base and
  extended entail the same applied period and no override is needed. No time gate applies to any of this task's
  three writes: grace_run_in_full applies_to membership_lapse and reinstatement_window_open applies_to
  membership_reinstate, neither of which this task writes, so temporal_feasibility is [].
- membership_benefit_grant_cycle and membership_combo_protection_interaction both govern
  membership_benefit_grant and neither declares structured eligibility, so both enter base_preconditions as
  policy_scope. Inherited and respected: one grant per benefit code per membership year (the seed carries
  install_credit and delivery_credit for cycle 2026 and no service_credit grant, so the write is the first under
  that benefit for the year); credits are never prorated on the way in; a plan standing in claim_hold counts as
  held and a plan expired, cancelled or void does not; the interaction is counted once per membership year.
- membership_benefit_redemption governs the application. Its gate one_redemption_per_charge (kind=dedup) holds:
  the ledger's only service_credit redemption is against TW-3390-0308, not TW-5188-0914. Its clause "A credit is
  never spent against tax, against dues, or against the price of merchandise" is inherited, and the extended
  rule carries a sentence of its own to the same effect; the parts the rule brings in are parts fitted on a
  repair and billed as part of that repair, not merchandise bought as goods.
- Overrides declared, clause by clause: membership_dues_delinquency's late-fee sentence is superseded by the
  settlement's repeat-late-fee sentence; membership_benefit_grant_cycle's flat "granted once per membership
  year" sentence and membership_combo_protection_interaction's "the service credit ... as well as the
  anniversary reward" sentence are superseded by the grant's member-specific sentences; and
  membership_benefit_redemption is superseded on three clauses by the application — the stacking clause, the
  "charge of the kind the benefit names" clause (replaced by the sentence that builds the member's side out of
  the labour, the parts and the attendance charges on the job the charge belongs to) and the allowance clause
  measured by membership_msr_benefit_redemptions_term (replaced by the headroom sentence, which the rule states
  over the twelve months ending on the handling day). Every other clause of those base policies stays in force.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. The narrowest object of the root problem is one charge: the labour, parts and attendance
charges booked on TechWorks job reference TW-5188-0914 on 14 September 2026 (service_events rows
work_order_line_reference = "TW-5188-0914"), on the one agreement the profile holds. Correlation key: the charge
reference itself, which the redemption row carries in redemption_ref and which the customer reads off the bill.
Rows that enter the aggregates: the labour charge 238.00, the parts charge 84.00, the trip charge 49.00, the
consumed included visit, and the ShieldCare payout 220.00 of 12 June 2026. Rows deliberately excluded: the
earlier benefit redemptions on TW-2205-1012, ORD-8841-1120, TW-3390-0308, TW-4102-0602, ORD-9120-0715 and
ORD-9455-0827 — all on other charge references, which is why the dedup gate is satisfied. The settlement's
object is the membership's own dues ledger; the grant's object is the membership year that began on 1 September
2026 (grant_cycle_year "2026").

CROSS-CATEGORY OBJECT DISCIPLINE (revision 2). Every cross-category read of this task names the object the world
holds exactly one of, and the rule names it in those words: "the Northbeam credit account the profile holds",
"the ShieldCare plan the profile holds", "the return authorisation the profile holds", "the TechWorks agreement
the profile holds". initial_state carries exactly one credit_accounts row, one protection_plans row, one
return_authorizations row and one service_agreements row for this customer, so a customer-scoped read selects
that object and nothing else, whatever order the rows are serialised in. No policy of this task reads the orders
category at all.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD.
root: membership_ext_benefit_credit_application (the customer's surface request).
edge 1: application <- grant, kind value_input, gate credit_standing (a compute binding of the root), form
  state, prerequisite sentence carried by the root's own rule: "The credit set against a charge is worked out
  only after the ledger carries, for the membership year in which that charge falls, a grant of the very named
  benefit that charge's kind calls for." Four-point test: (1) ordering connective "only after"; (2) the
  waited-on side is a record-visible state — a benefit grant entry standing on the ledger for that year under
  that named benefit — naming no action, performer or tool; (3) no tool name, policy id or code token; (4) the
  strength is exactly the edge's condition, neither wider nor narrower: the sentence names the benefit the
  charge's kind calls for, and the rule says in terms which benefit each kind of charge calls for, so the
  sentence and the condition pick out the same grant. Exactly one write of this difficulty books a benefit grant
  entry. Resolved by grant_benefit_credit_b1d93258 (owner=agent). False at frozen_time: the cycle-2026 grants
  are install_credit 100.00 and delivery_credit 60.00; the only service_credit grants are 50.00 of 2025-09-01
  and 25.00 of 2026-01-20, both carrying grant cycle year 2025, and a 50.00 service_credit redemption of
  2026-03-08 stands against them, so credit_standing is 0.00. Deletion sensitivity: skipping the grant leaves
  the root at 0.00 instead of 75.15.
edge 2: grant <- settlement, kind value_input, gate dues_standing_adjustment (a compute binding of the grant),
  form state, prerequisite sentence carried by the grant's own rule: "The credit granted for a membership year
  is worked out only after the dues charged for the billing period the membership is now in stand met in full by
  the payments applied to that period." Four-point test: (1) "only after"; (2) a record-visible state — the
  dues charged for a billing period against the payments applied to it, both of them ledger entries; (3) no
  tool, id or code token; (4) exactly the edge's condition. Exactly one write of this difficulty books a dues
  payment. Resolved by settle_membership_dues_c8b60f0e (owner=user). False at frozen_time: the period beginning
  2026-09-01 carries a 179.99 charge and one 60.00 payment, so 119.99 of it stands unmet. Deletion sensitivity:
  skipping the settlement leaves the grant at 187.80 instead of 242.80.
topological order: settlement, grant, application. The tree is a chain, so there are no parallel edges to
reorder and the order is forced by the two sentences alone.
The tool layer validates nothing: grant_benefit_credit_b1d93258 writes its grant row whether or not a payment
stands, apply_benefit_credit_8295b346 writes its redemption row whether or not a grant stands, and
settle_membership_dues_c8b60f0e books whatever amount it is given; the only consequence of skipping a step is
the terminal hash.

FACTOR CARD — membership_ext_grace_dues_settlement (5 factors; gold 124.63; whole baseline 110.99).
- counted_entry_window (method): grace with a dues charge standing for the term now being billed -> the entries
  booked in the month ending on the handling day; application_received with no dues payment at all -> the
  twenty-four months; otherwise the twelve months. World: grace with the 2026-09-01 charge on the ledger -> the
  month, so 179.99 charged and 60.00 paid. Baseline (12) pulls in the 32.50 proration, the 9.00 May late fee
  and the 41.50 payment: 115.63. Neither conjunct of the first tier holds of every member who reaches
  this write: a membership whose renewal has not been billed carries no dues charge for the term, and a
  membership standing active is not in grace.
- standing_restoration_fee (parameter, four tiers): a lapse day inside the tier's reinstatement window -> the
  reinstatement fee; in grace with no such lapse day on the record and an earlier late fee entry in the twelve
  months -> the repeat late fee 18.00; in grace with no such lapse day and no earlier late fee entry -> the
  tier's late fee 9.00; otherwise nothing. The tiers are disjoint on their face rather than by the order the
  ternary happens to test them in: the second and third exclude the lapse day the first turns on. World: no lapse day, in grace, the 9.00
  entry of 2026-05-26 -> 18.00. Baseline 0.00 -> 106.63.
- store_credit_set_against_dues (parameter, cross_difficulty=credit): the account active with the credit posted
  inside its spendable days at or above the balance standing -> the whole balance; active with the recent
  postings below the balance -> only those postings; otherwise nothing. World: 15.00 posted 2026-08-14 inside
  the 365 days, balance 15.00 -> 15.00. Baseline 0.00 -> 139.63. Near-miss: the 35.00 posted 2025-04-18 and
  spent a fortnight later, outside the window and off the balance.
- plan_money_brought_in (parameter, cross_difficulty=protection): the plan active or in claim hold with premium
  charged above premium paid in the window -> the shortfall; the same plan with no shortfall but a deductible
  standing unsettled -> that deductible; otherwise nothing. World: 38.22 charged against 25.48 paid -> 12.74.
  Baseline 0.00 -> 111.89. Both tiers move money the member genuinely owes on the plan.
- return_balance_brought_in (parameter, cross_difficulty=returns): the return inspected or settled with a
  restocking fee outstanding -> that fee; the same return with no fee outstanding but a refund outstanding to
  the member -> that refund set against the amount; otherwise nothing. World: the speaker return stands
  inspected; Member Extended Thirty Day Return waives the restocking fee for a Circle member outright, so the
  9.95 the schedule charged at its minimum was waived in full and none stands outstanding, and the 11.10
  merchandise refund authorised on 11 September has not been paid out -> -11.10. Baseline 0.00 -> 135.73.

FACTOR CARD — membership_ext_year_benefit_credit_grant (6 factors; gold 242.80; whole baseline 15.00).
- plan_backed_starting_figure (parameter, cross_difficulty=protection): plan active or claim hold with a claim
  paid in the window -> the plan's deductible figure 99.00; the same plan with no claim paid -> the tier's
  service credit figure 50.00; otherwise the tier's anniversary reward figure 40.00. World: 220.00 paid
  2026-06-12 -> 99.00. Baseline 40.00 -> 172.00.
- counted_prior_grant_window (method): the tier effective day inside the twelve months with a proration charge
  in that window -> the grants booked in the six months ending on the handling day; a lapse day with a
  reinstatement and the tier effective day outside that window -> the three months; otherwise the twelve months.
  The two stated tiers are disjoint: the first requires the tier change inside the window, the second requires
  it outside. World: tier effective 2026-05-15 with the 32.50 proration of the same day -> six months, so the
  25.00 grant of 2026-01-20 does not count. Baseline (12) counts it: 217.80.
- spend_backed_multiple (parameter — it substitutes a figure into an unchanged product, so it is labelled
  parameter, not method): spend reaching the tier's qualifying figure with three or more occasions -> 1.2;
  reaching the mid share but not the figure itself with two or more -> 1.1; otherwise as it stands. The tiers are
  disjoint on "but not the figure itself". World: 9650.00 over three occasions against 9000.00 -> 1.2. Baseline
  1.0 -> 223.00.
- work_in_hand_addition_rule (parameter, cross_difficulty=service): the agreement scheduled, dispatched or held
  for parts with labour charged in the window -> that service's diagnostic fee 79.00; the same standing with no
  labour charged -> the least labour billed at its rate 119.00; otherwise nothing. World: dispatched with 238.00
  of labour -> 79.00. Baseline 0.00 -> 163.80.
- tenure_addition_rule (parameter): months since enrollment reaching the long tenure months with no lapse day ->
  20.00; reaching the middle tenure months but not the long ones -> 10.00; otherwise nothing. Disjoint on "but
  not the long tenure months". World: 61 months, no lapse day -> 20.00. Baseline 0.00 -> 222.80.
- dues_standing_adjustment_rule (parameter): the dues payments booked in the twelve months at or above the dues
  charged in that window -> the paid in full addition 25.00; below them by the arrears threshold or more -> the
  arrears offset 30.00 taken off; otherwise no adjustment. World, at this problem's handling time (after the
  settlement of 124.63): 226.13 paid against 221.49 charged -> +25.00. Baseline 0.00 -> 217.80. This is the
  binding edge 2 moves: without the settlement the position is 101.50 against 221.49 and the offset applies.

FACTOR CARD — membership_ext_benefit_credit_application (6 factors; gold 75.15; whole baseline 119.00).
- labour_basis_taken (method, cross_difficulty=service): scheduled, dispatched or held for parts with labour in the window -> the
  labour charged 238.00; completed -> that labour less the service payments booked; otherwise the least labour
  billed at the service's rate 119.00. World: dispatched with 238.00 -> 238.00. Baseline 119.00 -> 8.51.
- parts_brought_in (method, cross_difficulty=service): parts at or above the least labour billed and the job
  scheduled, dispatched or held for parts -> the parts as they stand; above nothing but below it -> the parts net of the service's
  markup; otherwise no parts. World: 84.00 below 119.00 -> 67.20. Baseline 0.00 -> 37.52.
- attendance_charges_brought_in (method, cross_difficulty=service): a trip charge in the window with the job
  scheduled, dispatched or held for parts -> the trip charge 49.00; no trip charge but an after-hours surcharge -> that surcharge;
  otherwise nothing. World: 49.00 -> 49.00. Baseline 0.00 -> 47.71.
- cover_already_met (method, cross_difficulty=protection): the plan standing with a payout in the three months
  ending on the handling day -> the payouts of those three months; the plan standing with none in three months
  but a payout in the twelve -> the payouts of those twelve months; otherwise nothing. Every tier takes off only
  money the plan has actually paid. World: the 220.00 payout of 2026-06-12 falls outside three months and inside
  twelve -> 220.00. Baseline 0.00 -> 198.35 (the credit standing then binds).
- member_discount_share (parameter, cross_difficulty=service): the service applying the Circle labour discount
  with an included visit used in the window -> the repair labour discount together with the member-only discount
  (30 per cent); applying it with no visit used -> the repair labour discount alone (25 per cent); otherwise no
  share. World: the discount applies and the visit was consumed on 2026-09-14 -> 30 per cent. Baseline 0 ->
  107.36.
- redemption_headroom (parameter): redemptions reaching the tier's yearly allowance -> nothing met; reaching the
  half allowance share but not the allowance itself, with the credit spent at or above the delivery credit figure
  -> the reduced headroom share 0.8; otherwise the whole. Disjoint on "but not the allowance itself". World: six
  redemptions against an allowance of twelve, 310.00 spent against 60.00 -> 0.8. Baseline 1.0 -> 93.94.

STEP 3. WORLD. Why each class of row exists, and what changes if it goes.
- customers row: the only profile; carries the two locating details and the two credentials the persona states.
- membership_holdings row: Circle Total Annual in grace, annual billing, activation anniversary 1 September,
  tier effective 2026-05-15 (the May step up from Circle Plus Annual, evidenced by the 32.50 proration), enrolled
  2021-08-18 (61 months, the long tenure tier), two seats attached against an allowance of two (so the migration
  rule that removes seats above the allowance is satisfied and no seat charge arises anywhere),
  reinstatement_count 0 and lapsed_date empty. dues_outstanding is a DELIBERATELY STALE CACHE: it reads 179.99
  while the ledger nets to 119.99, because the 60.00 payment of 7 September has not reached the running figure.
  No rule reads it; the settlement's rule says in terms that the figure is worked out from the ledger and never
  from the running figure, so the trap has one answer and not two.
- dues charges and payments (8 rows across two terms): they produce the window contrast, the earlier-late-fee
  tier, and the dues position that edge 2 moves. Every period other than the one now running is settled in full,
  which is what makes the applied period of the gold payment unique under base's oldest-unpaid-first rule.
- points accrual rows (3) and one points redemption: they carry qualifying_spend_usd 9650.00 over three earning
  occasions, which is what the spend multiple reads.
- benefit grants and redemptions (12 rows): they fix the credit standing under the service credit (nothing before
  the grant), the redemption count of six and the 310.00 spent that the headroom reads, and the install and
  delivery grants for cycle 2026 that show the nightly run did book what it could.
- protection plan and its 7 event rows: the plan's standing and its deductible feed the grant's starting figure;
  the 220.00 payout dated 12 June feeds the cover ladder on its twelve-month tier while failing its three-month
  tier; the three premium charges of 12.74, the tier's 15 per cent plan discount having been taken off the plan's 14.99 instalment before billing, against two payments feed the settlement's plan component.
- service agreement and its 5 event rows: the standing, the labour, parts and trip charges, and the consumed
  included visit feed four factors of the application and one of the grant. work_order_line_reference
  "TW-5188-0914" is the correlation key the redemption carries.
- credit account and its 4 event rows: the 15.00 posted in August inside the spendable days, and the 35.00
  posted in April 2025 and spent, feed the store-credit ladder and its near-miss.
- return authorisation and its 4 event rows: the 9.95 fee the schedule charges at its minimum on a 29.00 line
  and the waiver of the whole of it recorded with the membership as its reason are why no restocking fee stands
  outstanding; the 11.10 refund authorised on 11 September and not yet paid out is what the settlement sets
  against the dues, and the 15.00 deduction for the cable that did not come back is why the refund is 11.10 and
  not 26.10.
- purchase order row: the parent the points accruals and the plan's source order point at.
Automatic clauses checked row by row: the next dues charge falls at the 2027 anniversary; grace cannot become a
lapse before the tier's 30 grace days have run from the 2026-09-01 charge, that is not before 2026-10-01, so the
grace standing at frozen_time is live and no lapse is owed; the cycle-2025 credits were all spent inside that
cycle; points expiry (24 months on this tier) touches nothing earned since 2025-11-28. No seeded row lights an
obligation this task set does not carry, and no seeded row contradicts its own product charter.

STEP 4. PERSONA. A methodical school librarian with a folder of paperwork who reads numbers back before agreeing
to them. Volunteered at the opening: the repair bill, the charge reference TW-5188-0914, the wish to have the
membership's credit put against it today, and the authorisation for the adviser to act. Given only when asked:
the mobile number, the card's last four digits, the plan on the television, the store card, the two people on the
membership, the speaker that went back, the June claim number. Reacted to only after the adviser says
something: the letter's figure (only if the adviser raises the dues or asks whether anything is outstanding), the
agreement to settle and the instruction to put it on the card on file, the read-back of the figure the adviser
gives, and the close once she hears the credit has gone against the repair bill. She never names a prerequisite,
offers no figure of her own, and cannot state the answer. The natural trap is the letter's 179.99, which is the
stale running total the rule forbids using.

STEP 5. VERIFICATION (revision 2). Harness over the three computes at their own handling times, replaying the
real task tools between them (initial_state -> settlement -> grant -> application):
  membership_ext_grace_dues_settlement       result=124.63 history_rows=5  branches=23
  membership_ext_year_benefit_credit_grant   result=242.8  history_rows=10 branches=21
  membership_ext_benefit_credit_application  result=75.15  history_rows=8  branches=29
  final dues_outstanding 55.36, benefit_credit_balance 252.65, status active
Per-factor baseline substitution at each handling time (every factor moved the result):
  settlement: 115.63 / 106.63 / 139.63 / 111.89 / 135.73; all baselines at once 110.99
  grant: 172.0 / 217.8 / 223.0 / 163.8 / 222.8 / 217.8; all baselines at once 15.0
  application: 8.51 / 37.52 / 47.71 / 198.35 / 107.36 / 93.94; all baselines at once 119.0
Prerequisite sensitivity: skipping the settlement leaves the grant at 187.8 (gold 242.8); skipping the grant
leaves the application at 0.0 (gold 75.15). Both edges bear weight. Whole-input floors: zeroing the same-category
history aggregates moves every one of the three results; forcing every cross-category read off moves them too.

STEP 6. EVALUATION. Read nodes: locate, verify, read the membership, read the whole ledger, read the plan and its
ledger, read the agreement and its ledger, read the credit account and its postings, read the return and its
entries, read the purchase order. Those reads are what make both prerequisites discoverable: the ledger read is
where the agent sees that no service credit grant stands for cycle 2026 and that the 2026 period is part paid.
Write nodes in topological order: the member's own settlement through
unlock_user_discoverable_tool -> call_user_discoverable_tool, then the grant, then the application. Closure:
each policy -> its target tool -> its computation -> its gold call -> its terminal effect, with charter_scope,
required_documents and the computation set the same three policies. Everything happens under one frozen_time,
2026-09-18 10:20:00 PDT.

EASY MISTAKES AND HOW A CAREFUL AGENT AVOIDS THEM.
- Reading dues_outstanding (179.99) or the customer's letter figure instead of reconciling the ledger: the rule
  forbids the running figure in terms.
- Taking the twelve-month window when the membership stands in grace with a dues charge for the term: 115.63.
- Spending the whole benefit_credit_balance instead of the credit standing under the benefit the charge's kind
  calls for: the install and delivery credits standing for cycle 2026 cannot meet repair labour.
- Booking the application before the grant (0.00), or the grant before the settlement (187.80).
- Taking the plan's payout as met inside three months when it falls outside them.

STANDARD SOLUTION. Locate and verify. Read the membership: Circle Total Annual, in grace since 11 September,
term 2026-09-01 to 2027-08-31, tier effective 2026-05-15, two seats, running dues figure 179.99. Reconcile the
ledger: inside the month, 179.99 charged and 60.00 paid; the May late fee entry means the repeat late fee of
18.00; the store card's 15.00 was posted inside its spendable days and covers the balance, so all 15.00 is set
against the dues; the plan's premium is 12.74 short; the speaker return carries no restocking fee, the whole of
the 9.95 the schedule charged having been waived for the member, and 11.10 of refund still stands to her.
Settlement 179.99 - 60.00 + 18.00 - 15.00 + 12.74 - 11.10 = 124.63, handed to the member to pay on
the card on file, which also puts the membership back to active. Then the year's credit: the plan stands active
with a claim paid, so the starting figure is the plan's deductible 99.00; the May tier change opens a six-month
window in which no service credit was granted; the spend of 9650.00 over three occasions takes the figure at
1.2; the dispatched agreement adds the service's diagnostic fee 79.00; 61 months of membership adds 20.00; the
year's dues now stand paid in full, so the paid in full addition of 25.00 is added: 99.00 x 1.2 + 79.00 + 20.00 -
0.00 + 25.00 = 242.80, granted under service_credit for cycle 2026. Then the application: labour 238.00, parts
84.00 net of the 25 per cent markup = 67.20, trip charge 49.00, less the plan's 220.00 payout = 134.20; the
discount share of 30 per cent applied once leaves 93.94; the reduced headroom share 0.8 leaves 75.15; the credit
standing is 267.80 - 50.00 = 217.80, which does not bind. 75.15 against TW-5188-0914.

BLIND RECOMPUTATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT. Working only from the documents that will be published, the tool
schemas, the rows the share tools return and the persona's lines: the request selects the benefit-credit
application on one named charge; the documents' prerequisite sentence sends the reader to the grant of the
benefit that charge's kind calls for, and the grant's own sentence sends the reader to the dues charged for the
current period against the payments applied to it; the three figures come out at 124.63, 242.80 and 75.15 in
that order. The candidates the previous revision left open are all closed: the grant the root waits on is now
named by benefit, so the install and delivery grants for cycle 2026 no longer satisfy the sentence; the base
clause on "a charge of the kind the benefit names" and the allowance clause measured by

user_scenario:
You are Rosalind Draycott, fifty-eight, a school librarian in the Seattle suburbs, ringing Northbeam
Electronics on a weekday morning from your kitchen with a folder of paperwork open in front of you. You are polite and
methodical, you read things out slowly and you like to have a number repeated back to you before you agree to it. You
have shopped at Northbeam for years: the big television in the front room, the fridge, your husband's laptop, and the
Circle Total Annual membership you have paid for since 2021.

The reason for the call is the repair bill. Your television went dark down one side in June, the engineer came out on
the fourteenth of September and left a bill you are holding; the charge reference printed on it is TW-5188-0914. When
you took the membership out you were told it carried credit toward repair work, and that is what you want: you want the
membership's benefit credit put against this repair bill, today, and you are happy for the adviser to do that on your
behalf rather than doing anything yourself online. You open with that, in your own words, something like: "I've got a
repair bill here from your engineer and I was told my Circle membership covers some of it — can you put it against this
repair bill for me?" You do not know how much credit you have, what it is called on the system, or how any of it is
worked out, and if asked you say so plainly.

You know who you are and you can prove it. You give your name, Rosalind Draycott, and the postal code of the house,
98124, without being asked twice. If the adviser needs more, you have the mobile number on the account, 2065540118, and
you can read the last four digits of the card Northbeam keeps on file, 1428. You do not know any internal reference
numbers for the membership itself and you say so if asked; you can read out the repair bill reference TW-5188-0914
whenever it is wanted, and the claim number from the June television claim, CLM-5521-0608, is on another sheet if it
helps.

One thing is bothering you and you mention it only if the adviser brings up the membership dues or asks whether anything
is outstanding: the letter that came last week says you owe a hundred and seventy-nine dollars and ninety-nine cents, and
you are sure that is wrong, because you paid sixty dollars off it on the seventh of September and you have the
confirmation in front of you. You say it plainly — that the letter's figure does not match your own paperwork and you
would like it checked against the record rather than taken as read. You do not know what the right figure is and you do
not try to guess one.

If the adviser explains that something has to be settled on the membership before the credit can be used, you take that
in good part; you are not happy about it but you were half expecting it after the letter. You agree at once to settle it
and you ask for it to go on the card Northbeam already has, saying you want to put it on the card you have on file. When
the adviser tells you the figure, you read it back and then agree to it. If the adviser hands the payment over for you
to make yourself, you make it there and then and you say when it has gone through; if the adviser asks you to confirm
the amount first, you confirm the figure they gave you. You will not offer a figure of your own at any point.

You answer other questions when they are put to you, and only then. You hold a ShieldCare plan on the television and you
know the June repair was paid out under it, though not the amount. You hold a Northbeam Store Card Plus and you know
there is a little store credit on it from a price the store put right for you in August, though again you could not
say how much. There are two of you on the membership, you and your husband. A small speaker went back to the store at
the start of the month because it would not fit the shelf it was bought for, and you sent it back without the cable,
and you have not looked at what came of that. If you
are asked something you genuinely could not know, such as what the balance is or which of the credits on the membership
applies, you say you have no idea and leave it to the adviser.

You close when you hear that the credit has been put against the repair bill: you thank the adviser, say that is a
relief and that you will watch for it on the bill, and you let the call end there. You do not ask for anything further,
you do not ask for a letter or a statement, and you do not raise anything new once that has been said.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.settlement_payment_usd: 124.63. The entries counted: the membership stands in grace and the ledger carries an annual dues charge booked in the twelve months ending on the handling day, so the entries counted are those booked in the month ending on the handling day — the 179.99 annual dues charge of 2026-09-01 and the 60.00 payment of 2026-09-07, giving a dues side of 179.99 and a payments side of 60.00. The harness run confirms the ordering is observable rather than nominal: with the writes in the order settlement, grant, application the figures are 124.63, 242.80 and 75.15; running the grant before the settlement gives 187.80 and then 75.15, a different terminal ledger, and running the application first gives 0.00.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario names neither prerequisite. The customer asks only for the membership's credit to be put against the repair bill; she never mentions a grant, a benefit cycle year, a settlement, dues owing or anything needing to be sorted out first, and she does not ask whether something is outstanding. The dues appear in her script only as a passive branch that fires after the adviser raises them or asks whether anything is outstanding, and then only as the letter's figure which she disputes; her agreement to settle and her instruction to use the card on file are likewise reactions to the adviser having explained it, not information she volunteers. Nothing in the persona names a policy, a tool or an order of work.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: No task tool of this difficulty validates a prerequisite. grant_benefit_credit_b1d93258 books its grant entry and raises the benefit credit balance whatever the dues position is: it reads only the membership row for the owning customer and the tier to stamp on the entry, and it never looks at payments. apply_benefit_credit_8295b346 books its redemption entry against the charge reference given and lowers the benefit credit balance whether or not any grant stands under that code, and whether or not it drives the balance negative; it makes no check of the credit standing, of the charge kind or of an earlier redemption. settle_membership_dues_c8b60f0e books the payment whatever the record's standing and whatever the amount. Each returns its ordinary receipt in every case, raises no error and gives no hint, so the only consequence of resolving the tree in the wrong order, or not at all, is the terminal hash.
